pos.personaBrief: Dynamo valued possession but played quick, vertical football and sat deep to counter Bayern in 1975; dominance came from danger created, not ball share (TFT 1975, Spielverlagerung).

pro.personaBrief: Lobanovskyi demanded a quick, vertical approach, long passes over the line from defenders and fast finishing after regains (Spielverlagerung 1986/88).

est.personaBrief: Interchangeable roles, defenders overlapping and attackers dropping back (Hard Tackle, TFT), inside a strictly planned system; width came from stretching the field in possession.

lar.personaBrief: Maslov abolished wingers for a 4-4-2 with wide midfielders; full-backs pushed up to provide width and the field was enlarged in possession, so width came from full-backs rather than classic wingers.

blo.personaBrief: Pressing from the off, immediate counterpress in the final third and sustained fitness for 90 minutes are the core of the school, with deliberate exceptions.

mar.personaBrief: Zonal marking replaced man-marking from Maslov onward; Lobanovskyi made opponent-specific exceptions such as man-coverage on Gullit in 1988.

pla.personaBrief: Lobanovskyi was a pragmatist adapting to each opponent, sitting deep when needed, and spoke of the dialectic of finding new strategies, while imposing his system on players.

res.personaBrief: Results over aesthetics: 'Games fade from the memory, but results stay', with pragmatic adaptation to what victory required.

sis.personaBrief: System over individuality: three Ballon d'Or forwards bought into it, everyone defends, football as a sum of efforts and a collective of believers.

jog.personaBrief: Fitness, nutrition and recovery underpinned sustained pressing; intensity is a basic requirement, with the classic idle number 10 unsuited to it.

bas.personaBrief: Lobanovskyi mixed signings with homegrown talent such as Baltacha and Beszonov; the aim was winning, with players chosen by fit to the system rather than age.

lid.personaBrief: Strict disciplinarian controlling every aspect of players' lives; the coach is the boss and stars follow the same rules.
